column2: CAP-1 · Design tokens: colour, spacing and radius as CSS variables
column3:
web/src/index.css is nearly empty on purpose, so the no-raw-hex rule is not broken on day
one. This ticket is what fills it. Every other frontend ticket in the project waits on it.

Acceptance criteria
* web/src/tokens.css defines colour, spacing, radius and the type scale as CSS custom
  properties.
* Light is the bare :root default. Dark is defined under BOTH [data-theme="dark"] and
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), so an explicit choice and the system default both work.
* A theme toggle in the shell flips data-theme on the root element and the choice survives a
  reload.
* No raw hex and no magic pixel value anywhere in web/src/ outside tokens.css. Add a check to
  ./run check that greps for one and fails.
* Every text-on-background pair meets WCAG AA contrast in both themes.

Blocks CAP-3, CAP-4, CAP-6, and every screen after them.

column2: CAP-2 · Typed API client with types generated from the contract
column3:
docs/openapi.yaml is the source of truth. A hand-written response type is how contract drift
becomes a runtime bug instead of a compile error.

Acceptance criteria
* npx openapi-typescript docs/openapi.yaml -o web/src/api/schema.ts, wired as
  npm run gen:types. The generated file is committed.
* One fetch wrapper in web/src/api/client.ts: attaches the bearer token, reads the base URL
  from VITE_API_BASE_URL, returns typed responses.
* Non-2xx unwraps the error envelope centrally into a typed ApiError carrying code, message
  and details, so callers switch on code rather than parsing strings.
* snake_case throughout. No mapping layer and nobody adds one.
* Verified against both the real API on :8000 and prism mock docs/openapi.yaml on :4010.
* TypeScript stays pinned to 6.x. openapi-typescript 7.13 crashes on TypeScript 7
  (openapi-ts issue #2841, open, no workaround). The generator picks the compiler version.

Blocks CAP-5 and every screen.

column2: CAP-3 · Core components, part one: Card, Button, Chip, Badge, Skeleton, ErrorNotice
column3:
Six of the ten components in the scope document. Build only the variants the screens need.

Acceptance criteria
* Badge covers draft, submitted and assessed. Chip covers selected and unselected, for the
  scope and sprint chips on the diary home.
* Skeleton is the loading primitive for every screen in the product. No spinners anywhere.
* ErrorNotice renders the error envelope's message, switches on code where it matters, and
  takes an optional retry action.
* All styling from tokens.css. Props are snake_case.
* A scratch route renders every component in every state so a reviewer sees them at once.

Depends on CAP-1.

column2: CAP-4 · Core components, part two: TextArea, ProgressBar, BottomSheet
column3:
The three components with behaviour in them rather than only appearance.

Acceptance criteria
* TextArea debounces on_change (600ms is a sensible start) and exposes saving / saved / failed.
  The entry stepper's autosave hangs off this, so get the failed state right, not just the
  happy one.
* ProgressBar renders "Competency 3 of 6" style progress from current and total props.
* BottomSheet is the container for the export and history sheets. Closes on Escape and on
  backdrop click, and traps focus while open.
* All styling from tokens.css.

Depends on CAP-1.

column2: CAP-5 · App shell: router, token context, role-aware navigation
column3:
The frame every screen mounts into.

Acceptance criteria
* React Router with a route per screen, each rendering a placeholder for now.
* Token context holds a bearer token, calls GET /auth/me once on boot, exposes the user.
* Navigation is built from what /auth/me returns. The client never decides a role itself.
  A hidden nav item is a convenience; the 403 is the rule.
* A switcher for the three seeded tokens. There is no login screen in the MVP (ADR #15).
* A 401 anywhere clears the token and returns to the token entry state.

Depends on CAP-2.

column2: CAP-6 · RadarPanel: axes and scale from props, never hardcoded
column3:
The product's headline visual, and the component definition-of-done items 4 and 5 both turn on.

Acceptance criteria
* A recharts RadarChart wrapped as RadarPanel, taking axes and domain as props. Never
  hardcoded to six axes or a four-point scale.
* Two series, self and counter-score, distinguishable in both themes and not by colour alone.
* Reads its shape from GET /me/radar.
* Verified against both seeded frameworks: La Trobe's six competencies on a flat 1-4, and
  SFIA 9, where each skill is valid over only part of the seven levels so the ranges are
  uneven. The scale comes from v_framework_scale, not from the component.
* Four states, including "not enough scores yet", which is different from empty.

Depends on CAP-1 and CAP-2. Blocks CAP-7.

The student's landing screen and the first place the radar appears in context.

Acceptance criteria
* Scope chips: all gigs, or one gig. Sprint chips appear once a gig is in scope.
* RadarPanel with a caption that changes with the scope, so it is always clear what the
  polygon is actually summarising.
* Entry list with status badges, linking through to the stepper.
* Export link opening the export sheet.
* All four states. Empty is a student with no reflections yet, and it says what to do next.

Depends on CAP-3, CAP-5, CAP-6.

Acceptance criteria
* Header with the gig, the assigned framework and the participant roles.
* Sprint list with opens_on and due_on, worded relatively where it helps: "due in 3 days",
  "not open yet". Sprints are a table rather than an integer precisely so this is possible.
* Diary card linking into the diary home scoped to that gig.
* All four states.

Depends on CAP-3, CAP-5.

column2: CAP-9 · DemoSeeder: reflections at every status, shaped scores, written narratives
column3:
Marked [~] in the scope document. Role holders, gigs, sprints and assignments are seeded and
the tokens are issued; the reflections are not, because nothing could write one until the
backend was finished. It can now. Every screen ticket after this is easier with real rows
behind it, and the client demo runs on this data.

Acceptance criteria
* Reflections in all three states: draft, submitted, assessed.
* Scores use a hidden ability profile per student, self-scores slightly optimistic and
  counter-scores closer to it, so the radar shows a real calibration gap instead of noise.
* Hand-written narratives, not lorem. These are read aloud at a client demo.
* Idempotent. Creates new rows rather than editing existing seeds, because five people share
  the instance and the seeds are fixed reference data.
* Never writes gig_key or sprint_key. Both are database-generated; keep them out of $fillable.
* ./run test and ./run smoke still pass afterwards.

No dependencies. Start day one.

The assessor's entry point, and the cheapest proof that authorisation resolves per gig.

Acceptance criteria
* Worklist from GET /review-queue with per-reflection progress: entries counter-scored over
  total.
* Scoped by gig. Sam is deliberately on one gig only, so this screen should show him one gig's
  work and Jane's token should not reach it at all.
* Links into the assessor stepper, a placeholder route until CAP-13.
* All four states. Empty means nothing is waiting, which is the normal state most of the time,
  so it should not look like an error.

Depends on CAP-3, CAP-5.
